jobs.description_text: Meet the Team Join Torc's System Integration & Enablement team, where we build the tools, test infrastructure, automation frameworks, and integration environments that enable Torc's autonomous driving platform to operate reliably at scale. Our team works at the intersection of hardware, embedded software, platform software, systems engineering, validation, and autonomy integration. We partner closely with teams across Compute Platform and the broader autonomy organization to improve the efficiency, repeatability, and quality of platform integration activities. We are looking for a Senior Systems Integration Engineer to lead on-truck platform bring-up and integration. You will be an engaged and collegial team member who is able to support reporters and editors across a range of responsibilities. Organization, flexibility and a desire to learn new skills are critical to success in this role. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office a minimum of four days each week. Responsibilities: Assist with data entry for poll collection pages Fact-checking and verifying figures in stories, charts and polling releases Gathering information and calling county officials to verify what data they will have on election night Help manage the audience accounts, i.e. generate, proofread and fact-check audience-related tasks Assisting in project management by keeping documentation and project boards up-to-date Monitor audience metrics for the weather team Eagerly tackle new responsibilities as the need arises Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world. jobs.title: Newsroom Operations Manager
jobs.description_text: The Role The New York Times is looking for an operational owner and highly organized self-starter to join our Newsroom Operations team as an Operations Manager. You will provide hands-on support and oversight of numerous logistics involved in the smooth daily operation of several assigned department(s) – News Platforms and Data, T Magazine and others. We are looking for a quick learner and creative problem solver who is capable of handling the ever-changing demands of a fast-paced newsroom environment. You will guide tasks across the finish line for the desks in the newsroom. Key to this will be supporting members of our masthead and our journalists with a variety of daily responsibilities and short- and long-term projects. This includes being at the center of on-the-ground coordination of both in-office and offsite events, ensuring execution of on-site logistics and meals for key news coverage events, ensuring that administrative operational tasks are completed by internal deadlines so that operations on the desk run continually and uninterrupted. You will report directly to a Senior Manager of Newsroom Operations. This role will be Hybrid, with a required in-office presence of 4 days a week. The schedule of these 4 days can fluctuate based on the needs of the desks, and during some peak news cycles, you may be required to be on site for 5 days during those weeks. Responsibilities: Serve as the primary, accountable operational contact for members of the masthead, department

jobs.title: Newsroom Strategy Manager
jobs.description_text: The New York Times Newsroom Strategy team is looking for a Strategy Manager with journalism, strategy and data experience to help shape and advance the newsroom’s biggest goals. This is an important and exciting moment to work in strategy at The Times. Our journalism has never been stronger or more relevant, and our newsroom continues to expand with an ever-wider array of beats, formats and expertise. At the same time, a rapidly changing media ecosystem presents significant opportunities as well as challenges, from changing audience habits to video and A.I. The Newsroom Strategy team works with Times leaders to help the newsroom chart and implement our strategy. From coverage to audience to operations, we help identify long-term opportunities, set priorities and accomplish them. The team has helped to shape our major recent video investment; expanded our journalism with new coverage initiatives and investments in areas like Live, Well and local; and partnered with teams like Audience and Security to strengthen critical parts of our journalism operation. As a Manager on the team, you will lead projects, undertake analysis and recommend paths forward to ensure we are maximizing our impact. You’ll take a reporter’s eye to The Times and our priorities — spotting and investigating opportunities and challenges — and develop plans to address them. jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description_text: The Role: The New York Times is looking for someone to join our Newsroom Operations team. We are looking for someone who can handle the demands of a fast-paced news environment and can work under sometimes ambiguous circumstances. The Operations Manager will work with Shows and Visuals, but also assist other departments at the center of visual journalism at The Times. The work of these journalists — along with visual efforts across the newsroom — is a pillar of our reporting that has a large and engaged audience. You will help support these journalists with a variety of daily responsibilities and short- and long-term projects and coordinate with this group's other operations managers. You will be responsible for ensuring that day-to-day on-site operational tasks are completed in a timely manner to support the needs of department managers and staff. The Operations Manager's work is critical in supporting the journalism produced at The New York Times and all tasks, whether daily, weekly or one-off are greatly valued. You will report to a senior manager of Newsroom Operations. This role will be Hybrid, with a required in-office presence of 4 days a week. The schedule of these 4 days can fluctuate based on the needs of the desks, and during some peak news cycles, you may be required to be on site for 5 days during those weeks. jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager, News
jobs.description_text: The New York Times is looking for a motivated, collaborative, creative, analytical, and user-centric product marketer to help deepen audience engagement with our News product, with a particular focus on community and sharing features in the core Times app. Reporting to the Director of Product Marketing, News, you will be embedded within the Community News Product team as the dedicated product marketing lead. You will partner closely with product, design, and newsroom stakeholders to leverage our community and sharing experiences to drive daily habit and new audience growth. Your core focus will be the Community News Product team, with opportunities to support other editorially driven News product teams as priorities require. You will combine strategic leadership with hands-on execution: helping shape the product roadmap, developing go-to-market strategies, leading cross-functional launches, and creating lifecycle marketing programs that help our readers feel connected to our journalism, our newsroom, and each other. This role is a hybrid position, where you'll be in the office three times per week in our NYC Headquarters. Responsibilities: Act as the embedded product marketing lead for the Community News Product team, partnering with product, design, and newsroom stakeholders to define the role of commenting, community features, and sharing in the News product experience. Partner with editors, reporters, and newsroom leadership to increase journalist participation in comments

jobs.title: Research Director, Audience Insights, Content Insights
jobs.description_text: About the Role, Mission or Department Overview The Research Director, Content Insights will have a critical role informing the creation, iteration and measurement of video and video products at the New York Times. You will lead all video measurement research to inform our understanding of how video content performs across platforms, surfaces, and audience segments. You will oversee the end-to-end measurement of video effectiveness, from individual videos to longer-form recurring concepts, and translate data into relevant strategies that inform production, distribution, and editorial decisions. You will also work with product, design, and editorial teams to improve on-platform video experiences. You will report to the Managing Director, News Products on the Audience Insights Team and will collaborate with partners across the Newsroom. You understand how to blend market research and user research methods and practices into actionable insights for an entire mission. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week. Responsibilities: Develop audience research to support the creation and growth of video franchises and recurring shows. Drawing on research methods used by production studios and streaming networks, you'll conduct research that can inform greenlight decisions — including concept testing, pilot testing, audience appetite studies, and competitive landscape analysis. Partner with video leaders

jobs.title: Research Lead, Wirecutter
jobs.description_text: About the Role, Mission or Department Overview We are looking for a Research Lead with experience ensuring that shopping-centric insights are at the heart of product development. You will lead a variety of end-to-end research projects that inform Wirecutter's strategy. Your projects will focus on helping connect our visitors to Wirecutter across the full shopping experience. Your research will inform audience strategy, content prioritization, and the Wirecutter Store, amongst other areas. You will be an important partner with Design, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Data, Editorial, guiding decision-making and informing the teams' strategies. We at The New York Times seek the truth and help people understand the world. This mission is rooted in our belief that great journalism has the power to make each reader's life richer and more fulfilling, and all of society stronger and more just. The mission of the New York Times Audience Insights team is to help The Times grow by understanding our audience. The Audience Insights team is a team of researchers that employ tools, methods and approaches across a wide variety of research domains, including product, human-centered design, innovation, market and UX research, and we draw from principles in the social sciences (Psychology, Anthropology, Sociology and Behavioral Economics). jobs.description_text: About the Role, Mission or Department Overview We are looking for analytical talent to turn experience with data and support of world-class journalism into decision-making insights. As part of the Data and Insights Group (DIG) and Data Platforms, you will join a large community of accomplished data professionals who partner with Product, Engineering, and Design teams across the business. You will focus on supporting our enterprise partners and report to our Executive Director, Analytics Engineering. Responsibilities: You will independently lead work streams in a high leverage, high visibility role building the next generation of data foundations for our core enterprise reporting datasets that executives depend on daily You will be our subject matter expert on our subscription data, translating our needs into technical implementations and mentoring teammates on the domain You will design reusable business logic and data pipelines allowing other analysts and partners to answer questions quickly. You will develop data models, data contracts, alerting, context, and metrics/semantic layers supporting both traditional and AI-assisted analytical use cases. Basic Qualifications: 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, product analytics or similar data-intensive roles Proficiency in SQL, DBT, and data transformation workflows Proficiency in Python for ETL and analytics use cases Experience communicating updates and resolutions to customers and other partners

This role sits within the Games marketing vertical and reports to the Associate Creative Director , Games, Marketing. You will work closely with other marketing creative team members (writers, designers and our audio and video teams), as well as partners in marketing and media strategy, product design, audience insights and brand identity to bring to life campaigns across the marketing funnel that drive performance while upholding a high bar for design craft. You are responsible for driving creative ideation , execution and production of marketing assets, as well as helping evolve the design systems, libraries and templates that support experimentation at scale. You bring a refined aesthetic, a nuanced understanding of typography, layout and color, motion design and strong design craft skills. We want an individual who is not only just a stellar designer, but also idea‑focused and can do the work of efficiently bringing their ideas to life in a way that inspires and excites others, and then presents them effectively and enthusiastically. This is a temporary 6 month role reporting to the Associate Creative Director , Marketing, Games. It can be either remote within the US or hybrid in our NYC offices. jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Games Mobile Apps
jobs.description_text: About the Role: The New York Times is looking for a Senior Engineering Manager, reporting to the Director of Engineering, Games Platform, to lead a team focused on our mobile platform. In this role, you will lead and support engineers and collaborate with cross functional partners to deliver and maintain the premier destination for digital puzzle games. This position is key to building the next generation of our Games app across iOS and Android. We see value in continued investment in Games as a standalone subscription opportunity and a valuable member of the overall NYTimes bundle, which also includes News, Cooking, Wirecutter and The Athletic. We view our mobile platform as the best opportunity for Games to continue driving engagement with our product, in addition to driving subscription growth. NYT Games is a supportive and collaborative team that values inclusion, diversity and personal growth. We combine exceptional product development with a world-class suite of puzzles including beloved titles such as the NYT Crossword, Spelling Bee, Connections, Crossplay and Wordle. Come help us on our journey to grow a world-class mobile platform, as we continue delivering delightful experiences to millions daily. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 2-3+ days/week. jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Wirecutter
jobs.description_text: About the Role: Wirecutter, the product review and shopping guide arm of The New York Times Company, is looking for an experienced Senior Engineering Manager for Wirecutter's Growth team. You will lead the engineers who build experiences that grow and strengthen our direct relationship with readers. The team's work includes search discovery, registration, newsletters, and distribution across The New York Times and other platforms. This role reports to the Wirecutter VP of Engineering. Every year, Wirecutter reaches millions of users and drives billions of dollars in sales for our merchant partners. Through rigorous testing, research, and reporting across hundreds of merchants, our dedication to helping people find the best products remains as relevant today as it did over ten years ago. We deliver human-generated, straightforward recommendations that inspire readers while saving them time, effort, and money. Hybrid work (from home and in-office) is preferred for this role, although full-time remote applicants will also be considered. As a hybrid employee, you can typically expect to come into our New York City headquarters two days each week. jobs.title: Senior Manager, Audience & Product Analytics, NYT Wirecutter
jobs.description_text: About the Role New York Times Wirecutter team is looking for a Senior Manager, Audience & Product Analytics to power our growth strategy. Your core mandate will be to build an understanding of our audience— who they are, how they engage with content and product features, and what brings them back. You will lead a team of analysts responsible for understanding audience trends, driving product improvement, and optimizing user engagement. You will provide leadership and data-driven insights, working with audience, product, and engineering leads to establish goals, design experiments, and uncover new opportunities. You will report to the Executive Director of Data Analytics and Insights, Wirecutter. This opportunity is flexible to in office or remote work. Responsibilities You will manage a team of three direct reports—promoting a culture of curiosity and excellence while setting clear deliverables, supporting career growth, and ensuring high-quality analytics output You will analyze audience growth, traffic drivers, customer journey touch points, and user engagement trends to inform strategic decision-making. You will partner with functional leads (Product, Design, Engineering, Editorial) to set strategy, define goals, and build the audience and product analytics roadmap. You will lead the design, execution, and post-analysis of product experiments (A/B testing). This is a high impact leadership role, and you will be measured by your ability to build a cohesive physical security architecture, improve how our colleagues work together, and ensure our corporate security program supports the company's growth. jobs.description_text: About the Role NYT Wirecutter is looking for a Senior Manager, Revenue Analytics to power our business strategy. Your core mandate is to increase audience monetization across our primary businesses—Affiliate, Advertising, and E-commerce—ensuring we preserve long-term audience trust. As a player-coach role, you will lead a team of analysts and partner closely with Revenue, Product, and Marketing leads to establish KPIs, run conversion experiments, and build attribution frameworks that scale revenue. You will report to the Executive Director, Data Analytics. Responsibilities You will lead, mentor, and onboard a team of two direct reports, nurturing their career growth You will analyze affiliate revenue drivers (e.g., merchant commissions, EPC, conversion rates, and partner yield) across all content touch points. jobs.title: Senior Manager, UX Writing
jobs.description_text: About Us Marketing plays a key role in extending the journalistic legacy and mission of The Times into the future. Our job is to answer the question: “Why is quality journalism worth paying for?” We create award-winning marketing that builds awareness of our brand and affinity for the breadth of our journalistic offering. Above all, we strive to be timely, straightforward and relevant in our marketing — illustrating in new and creative ways how The New York Times can enrich the lives of our readers. About The Role In an ongoing effort to create new and elevated product experiences, we’re looking for a Senior Manager, UX Writing to concept, develop and execute UX writing across The New York Times portfolio, including our core news product and Games, Cooking, Wirecutter and The Athletic. You will write crisp, clear and engaging copy for customer journeys, partnering with product, design, marketing, engineering, research and editorial teams to create experiences that grow, engage and retain subscribers. You will also manage a small team of freelance UX writers, coordinating resources, assigning projects and developing practical standards and workflows. We're looking for candidates who can balance the clarity that UX copy demands with the personality and approachability of an engaging brand.
